annotations.title: Check the whole app before deploying

description: Check how the app uses the chart library, before every deploy and after check_chart: reads the app's own source (never the files generate_chart and setup_fabric_app wrote) and reports, each with file, line and the library call to use instead: hand-written selection glue (a toggle, a second-click guard, a remount to clear) where useBicFilter + selects does it; row positions read from the DOM; the payload's __rowIdx__ / __geo* columns built by hand; a slider beside a chart that draws its own controls (useBicControls); notes kept but never shown on the marks (annotations); a chart outside a BicChartPanel, a fixed height below the panel's minimum, a flex-1 container without min-h-0 / min-w-0; two charts setting the same element id; and @bicharts / Rayfin / Fabric visuals packages behind npm's latest. It also draws every chart under src/charts the way check_chart does and reports any that throw, come out blank or don't pass a click to onSelect. Local and free; npm is only asked for versions, and a stack finding is skipped when npm can't be reached. Layout findings are WARNINGS: a static read can't prove a layout. Fix the app's own files; regenerate a chart rather than edit its generated code.

check_npm.description: Compare the stack with npm's latest (default true).

draw_charts.description: Also draw every chart under src/charts (default true).

project_dir.description: The app's folder. Defaults to the folder setup_fabric_app used, else the working directory or the one project folder inside it.
